citations.quote: $$\partial_t\bar u+\operatorname{div}(\bar u\otimes\bar u)+\nabla\bar p=\nu\Delta\bar u+\bar f-\operatorname{div}R.$$

A **material motion** is a map $\chi\in C^2(I\times U,\mathbb R^3)$ such that each $\chi_t=\chi(t,\cdot)$ is a bijection from $U$ onto an open image, has a $C^2$ inverse, and has positive Jacobian determinant; in the initial chart set $\chi(0,a)=a$. The label $a\in U$ and position $x=\chi(t,a)$ are measured in metres.
The Eulerian velocity is the vector field defined by $u(t,\chi(t,a))=\partial_t\chi(t,a)$, measured in m s$^{-1}$.

For a stress tensor $\sigma$, use the tension-positive convention in which the traction (force per unit current area) on a surface with outward unit normal $n$ is $\sigma n$. Set $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i=\partial_j\sigma_{ij}$; the tensor contraction is $S:T=\sum_{i,j}S_{ij}T_{ij}$. Stress and traction have units Pa $=\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$.

derivations.claim: For each fixed $t$, $\chi_1(t,\cdot)$ and $\chi_2(t,\cdot)$ are translations with inverses $x\mapsto x-ct e$ and $x\mapsto x+ct e$, respectively; $D_a\chi_j=I_3$ and $J_j=1$. They are $C^2$ on $I\times U$, orientation preserving, and equal the identity at $t=0$. Since $c$ has units m s$^{-1}$ and $t$ has units s, the translations preserve the stated metre coordinates. By [F2]–[F3], their Eulerian velocities on the images are $ce$ and $-ce$, as extended by the same constant fields to $\Omega$. Each field is $C^\infty$, divergence free, time independent, and has constant $u_j\otimes u_j$; hence every derivative in the per-unit-mass member equation is zero, so the hypotheses of [F1] hold with the given zero pressure, forcing, and viscosity.
The equal-weight mean is $\bar u=(ce-ce)/2=0$, so $v_1=ce$ and $v_2=-ce$. Therefore $R=\tfrac12(ce\otimes ce)+\tfrac12((-ce)\otimes(-ce))=c^2e\otimes e$.

For every $z\in\mathbb R^3$, $z^{\mathsf T}Rz=c^2(z\cdot e)^2\ge0$, and $R$ is symmetric and nonzero. Since each velocity has units m s$^{-1}$ by [F3], $R$ has units m$^2$ s$^{-2}$; multiplying by $\rho_0$ in kg m$^{-3}$ gives kg m$^{-1}$ s$^{-2}$=Pa. Thus $\sigma_R=-\rho_0R$ is a negative-semidefinite effective correction with units Pa under [F4].

The supplier equation [F1] contains $-\operatorname{div}R$ on the right. Multiplying by the constant $\rho_0$ gives $-\rho_0\operatorname{div}R=-\operatorname{div}(\rho_0R)=\operatorname{div}(-\rho_0R)$, because $\rho_0$ is spatially constant. Under [A2] the corresponding effective stress correction is therefore $\sigma_R=-\rho_0R$; the covariance $R$ itself remains positive semidefinite.
